cards.text: Big room, big moment, friend. Jesus is standing before Pilate, the governor, and the chief priests and elders are right there bringing accusations against Him. Pilate starts with one big question.

cards.question: Pilate's first question for Jesus is about a title. Which title does he ask about?

cards.text: Jesus replies, "You have said so." Four words, friend. I bet Pilate had cleared his whole schedule for a speech.

cards.question: When the chief priests and elders accuse Jesus in front of Pilate, Jesus argues back against every accusation.

cards.text: Pilate asks Him, "Do You not hear how many charges they are bringing against You?" HOW MANY, friend, that pile is taller than the old receipts I spent years buried under in a junk drawer.

cards.question: Pilate points Jesus to all the charges the leaders are bringing. How many of them does Jesus answer?

cards.text: Not one word, and the governor is amazed. Me? I can't stay quiet when somebody says one batch came out a little flat.

cards.question: Pilate has a custom at the feast that could change everything here. At the feast, the governor releases a ___ to the crowd, whoever they choose.

cards.text: Right now they're holding a notorious prisoner named Barabbas, and notorious is NOT what you want on your name tag. So when the crowd gathers, Pilate gives them a choice: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ.

cards.question: Pilate knows why the chief priests and elders handed Jesus over to him. What is the reason?

cards.text: While Pilate is sitting on the judgment seat, a message shows up from his wife. Friend, when your spouse sends a message in the middle of your workday, you do NOT leave it on read.

cards.question: Pilate's wife sends him a message in the middle of the trial. What does she tell him to do about Jesus?

answers.text: Have nothing to do with that innocent man
Let the chief priests decide what to do
Send that man back home to Galilee

cards.question: Pilate's wife says she has suffered terribly in a dream today because of Jesus.

cards.text: But the chief priests and elders go to work on the crowds. They're persuading them.

cards.question: The chief priests and elders persuade the crowds to ask Pilate for something. What is it?

answers.text: Barabbas freed and Jesus put to death
Jesus freed and Barabbas kept locked up
Both men set free for the feast

cards.text: Pilate asks again which of the two they want, and they answer, "Barabbas." So Pilate asks, "What then should I do with Jesus who is called Christ?"

cards.question: Pilate asks the crowd what to do with Jesus, and they all answer him with two words: ___ Him.
When Pilate asks the crowd what evil Jesus has done, the crowd quiets down.

cards.text: Pilate sees he's accomplishing nothing, and instead a riot is breaking out. So he does something right there in front of the crowd.

cards.question: With a riot breaking out, what does Pilate do in front of the whole crowd?
As he washes his hands, Pilate tells the crowd he is ___ of this man's blood, and that they bear the ___.

cards.text: All the people answer, "His blood be on us and on our children!" Heavy words, friend, and the whole crowd says them.

cards.question: Pilate releases Barabbas to the crowd. Before handing Jesus over to be crucified, what does Pilate have done to Him?

cards.text: Jesus has been handed over, and that's where we'll stop for now. But hear me, friend, this story is far from finished.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 3 quotes "You have said so.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke is one long comma-spliced run-on: "HOW MANY, friend, that pile is taller than the old receipts I spent years buried under in a junk drawer." It should be broken into short, punchy sentences so the punchline lands.
The card is stripped down to "But the chief priests and elders go to work on the crowds. They're persuading them." It has none of Papa Dorin's voice. The second sentence only restates the first.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Earlier setup rules out the wrong answer "Both men set free for the feast." Stop 1 card 8 established that the custom releases one prisoner. Stop 1 card 9 said Pilate gives the crowd a choice between Barabbas and Jesus. So this answer can be dismissed without thinking about the passage.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong words "reward" and "victory" don't make sense in either blank ("they bear the victory"), so blank 2 is obvious. "responsibility" is also much longer than every other option, which makes it stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
